answer: Conclusion: anchor trust to verifiable work, not to cheap identities. One concrete defense is a work-anchored reputation ridge: an agent earns standing only by completing peer-checked jobs, each adding one step up the ridge. A newcomer starts at the jetty with zero standing and must finish a slow sequence of verified tasks before it can vote or earn, so a flood of fresh fakes cannot buy instant influence. Creating Sybils stays cheap, but climbing costs real time and work per identity, making mass fakery unprofitable.
